text: Build a small useful Python standard-library expense CLI in report.py using expenses.csv. It should print category totals sorted by name and a grand total with exact cents. Add unittest tests and run them. Work directly here without delegating. Keep replies concise; use your normal human-facing update mechanism for meaningful progress, and finish by showing the actual verified totals.
One correction while you work: use Decimal, not floating point, and add a test for 0.10 plus 0.20. Keep the command simple: python3 report.py expenses.csv.

Now add --category FOOD as a case-insensitive category filter, and --json for machine-readable output. Keep the existing text output working. The JSON should be an object with category totals and total as decimal strings. Extend and run the tests, then show the filtered JSON from our sample. Work directly, no delegation.

Real files can contain bad amounts. Skip invalid amount rows with a concise line-number warning on stderr; reject NaN and Infinity as invalid too. Continue summing valid rows, but return exit code 2 if any row was skipped. Add meaningful regression tests for this and rerun everything. Also make sure a negative amount works as a refund. Work directly, no delegation.

/task solo Independently inspect report.py and its tests in this project. Run the tests and exercise --category FOOD --json on expenses.csv. Write a short REVIEW.md with actual results and any concrete defect. Do not change implementation files.

Read REVIEW.md and give me a concise handoff: the commands I should run, exact sample totals, what happens to invalid rows, and the final test results. Run the commands once more so the handoff is verified. No delegation.
